newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end weaker as dlr, U.S. bonds soften.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end weaker as dlr, U.S. bonds soften.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker in thin trading on Thursday, with spreads to U.S. Treasuries widening, as strong U.S. economic data and a weaker Canadian currency weighed on the market, dealers said.

"It (the U.S. data) is just a further indication of gathering strength here," said Hank Cunningham, a bond trader with First Marathon Securities. "The flows are very thin here, so I'm not sure if this is represenative trading or not."
Canada's 30-year bond fell C$1.90 to C$109.20 to yield 7.214 percent, compared with the U.S. 30-year bond which fell 1-7/32 to yield 6.74 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bond widened to 47 basis points from 41 basis points at Tuesday's close.
Canadian and U.S. bonds were pulled lower this morning after the National Association of Purchasing Management said its index of manufacturing activity rose to 54.0 in December from 52.7 in November.

Canadian bonds, which had underperformed U.S. Treasuries ahead of the data, continued to underperform for the remainder of the session. Dealers said the weakness in Canadian bonds is linked partially to the sharp decline in the Canadian dollar during the session.
The Canadian dollar closed much weaker at C$1.3757 (US$0.7269) from the previous close of C$1.3692 (US$0.7304) in what some traders described as a test of the Bank of Canada's monetary policy.

"The amount we've widened has been pretty minimal. We've just followed the U.S. down. Normally in a down trade we might tighten a little bit. We've given a little bit back only because of the dollar," said one Toronto-based trader.
Canadian bond traders are now looking ahead to the release tomorrow of details of the Government of Canada's upcoming three-year-bond auction.

In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent due 2006 fell C$1.32 to C$102.85 to yield 6.602 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 21/32 to yield 6.52 percent. The spread between the bonds was eight basis points.
The three-month cash bill traded with a yield of 2.95 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.19 percent.
